title: When the loop must stop
scenario: A studio runs a make-and-review loop for a 30-second tea ad. The ad did not pass. You decide what the stop rules should have been. The settings, the log and the notes are made up for this case.
exhibit:
SETTINGS (ours, made up for this case)
  Pass:     all 4 rubric lines pass.
  Tries:    Claude outcome, max_iterations = 3.
  Budget:   $40 per ad. One round (new clips + review) costs about $12.
  Deadline: client call, Friday 15:00.

REVIEW LOG (made up for this case)
  Round 1  line 3 FAIL (lid is brown in shot 4)   round cost $12   total $12
  Round 2  line 3 FAIL (lid is brown in shot 4)   round cost $12   total $24
  Round 3  line 3 FAIL (lid is brown in shot 4)   round cost $12   total $36
           result: max_iterations_reached

TEAM NOTES (made up)
  Dev:  "Raise max_iterations to 50 so the ad always passes."
  Ops:  "The OpenAI version of this agent uses max_turns = 3, the same as
         Claude's 3, so the limits are the same."
  OpenAI run (other job): hit max_turns and raised MaxTurnsExceeded.

questions.prompt: The log ends with max_iterations_reached. What does it mean for the ad?

options.text: The ad passed every line, and the agent stopped because there was nothing left to fix
options.explanation: If the rubric had passed, the result would be satisfied. Line 3 failed in every round.

options.text: The loop ran out of tries, so the ad is not approved and a person must look at it
options.explanation: Right. Claude's docs say one final turn follows and no further evaluation runs. Out of tries does not mean passed.

options.text: The grader failed because the rubric did not fit the ad, so the rubric must be thrown out
options.explanation: That is the failed result. Here the grader worked, and the same line failed each time.

options.text: The agent will keep trying quietly in the background, until the money for the job is gone
options.explanation: The docs say no further evaluation runs after this result. The session goes idle.

questions.prompt: Line 3 failed with the same reason in all three rounds. Which stop rule would have saved money?

options.text: A no-progress rule: if the same line fails twice in a row, stop and hand over to a person
options.explanation: Right. This rule is ours, not a vendor's. After two identical failures, round 3 was likely wasted, and it cost $12.

options.text: A rule that doubles the number of tries after each failure, to give the agent more chances
options.explanation: More tries after a repeated failure only spend more. The maker was not learning from the notes.

options.text: A rule to lower the pass bar after round 2, so that the ad passes without line 3
options.explanation: Dropping a rubric line to get a pass hides the fault. The lid would still be brown.

options.text: A rule to ask the grader to be more polite, so that the maker takes the feedback better
options.explanation: The grader's tone is not the problem. The maker did not change the lid.

questions.prompt: The cap is $40 and a round costs about $12. How many rounds may start before the budget rule stops the agent?

options.text: Four, because three rounds cost $36 and the fourth is allowed to use up the rest of it
options.explanation: A fourth round would bring the total to $48, which is over the $40 cap.

options.text: Two, because the agent must always keep half of its budget unspent for the hand-over
options.explanation: Nothing in the exhibit asks for half of the budget to be kept back. Three rounds fit in $40.

options.text: As many as the tries setting allows, because the budget is only a hint for the producer
options.explanation: A budget rule is a stop rule. It ends the loop even if tries are left.

options.text: Three: they cost $36 in total, and a fourth round would reach $48, which is over the cap
options.explanation: Right. The rule stops before a round that would break the cap. The numbers are made up for this case.

questions.prompt: The dev wants max_iterations = 50 "so the ad always passes." What is wrong with this?

options.text: Nothing is wrong, since more rounds always lead to a better ad, up to 50 rounds in total
options.explanation: More rounds do not fix a failure that repeats, and each one adds cost.

options.text: Nothing is wrong with fifty, because max_iterations counts dollars, so it sets a $50 budget cap
options.explanation: max_iterations counts grade-and-revise rounds, not money. Its maximum is 20. For money you need your own budget rule.

options.text: Claude's default is 3 and its maximum is 20, so 50 is not allowed, and more rounds cost more
options.explanation: Right. Claude's docs say max_iterations is optional, with default 3 and maximum 20. Extra rounds also add cost.

options.text: The setting only works for text outputs, so it cannot be used for a video ad at all here
options.explanation: The docs show the setting for any outcome. It is not limited to text.

questions.prompt: Ops says OpenAI's max_turns = 3 is "the same" as Claude's 3. What do you say?

options.text: They differ: OpenAI counts model calls, and Claude counts grade-and-revise rounds
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI's docs describe a turn as an agent-loop turn, meaning an LLM call. Claude's iteration is a round of evaluation and revision.

options.text: They are the same, because both vendors count the number of times a person approves
options.explanation: Neither count is about person approvals.

options.text: They differ only in name, because both count the dollars spent in each loop round
options.explanation: Neither limit counts money. For money you need your own budget rule.

options.text: They are the same, because all vendors use the same unit for every limit they offer
options.explanation: Vendors count different things. Check what a limit counts before copying a number.
